textbookBox.concept: A decimal like 27.53 has 2 tens, 7 ones, 5 tenths and 3 hundredths. Fractions with denominators 10, 100, 1000 and so on are easy to write as decimals.

beats.en: A decimal like 27.53 has 2 tens, 7 ones, 5 tenths and 3 hundredths. Fractions with denominators 10, 100, 1000 and so on are easy to write as decimals.

beats.en: Arshad buys 5 pens at ₹9.5 each. Adding 9.5 five times gives 47.5, so 9.5 × 5 = 47.5. A car runs 12.5 km on 1 litre. On 7.5 litres it covers 12.5 × 7.5 = 93.75 km.
beats.speakEn: Arshad buys 5 pens at 9 rupees.5 each. Adding 9.5 five times gives 47.5, so 9.5  times  5  equals  47.5. A car runs 12.5 km on 1 litre. On 7.5 litres it covers 12.5  times  7.5  equals  93.75 km.

textbookBox.concept: With counting numbers the product is at least as big as both numbers. With decimals this is not always so. When both numbers are greater than 1, the product is greater than both: 3.4 × 6.5 = 22.1.

beats.en: With counting numbers the product is at least as big as both numbers. With decimals this is not always so. When both numbers are greater than 1, the product is greater than both: 3.4 × 6.5 = 22.1.
beats.speakEn: With counting numbers the product is at least as big as both numbers. With decimals this is not always so. When both numbers are greater than 1, the product is greater than both: 3.4  times  6.5  equals  22.1.

beats.en: Anuja cuts a 3.9 m ribbon into 10 equal pieces. 3.9 is 39/10, and dividing by 10 is multiplying by 1/10, so each piece is 39/100 = 0.39 m. Cut into 100 pieces, each is 0.039 m, which is 3.9 cm or 39 mm.
beats.speakEn: Anuja cuts a 3.9 metres ribbon into 10 equal pieces. 3.9 is 39/10, and dividing by 10 is multiplying by 1/10, so each piece is 39/100  equals  0.39 metres. Cut into 100 pieces, each is 0.039 metres, which is 3.9 centimetres or 39 mm.
